newsitem.title: UK: European 7 bln stg frigate project in danger - paper.
newsitem.headline: European 7 bln stg frigate project in danger - paper.

text.p: Disagreement between the UK, France and Italy over a seven billion stg joint programme to build Navy frigates has put the so-called Horizon programme in jeopardy, said a report in the Financial Times on Monday.

The report said disagreement had broken out between the three countries over the ship designs and capability and that if a resolution was not found by the end of March each would have to revert to a more expensive route of separate national designs.

The frigates are intended to protect shipping from missile or aircraft attack. But the UK wants a wider capability, said the report. Horizon should be able to protect a convoy of merchant vessels or warships spread over a wide area without the need for an aircraft carrier as back-up, according to the UK view.
But France, which had initially supported this view, now wants a cheaper option following cuts in its military budget. It is backed by Italy in calls for a cheaper and simpler frigate, said the FT.

The ships are needed by 2004 resulting in intense pressure for a speedy decision. The news is of concern to the private sector, with a prime contractor shipyard appointed in each of the three countries.
GEC-Marconi's Yarrow shipyard heads up the UK team with British Aerospace and Vosper Thorneycroft also involved.
